dataset.name: NGEE Arctic Tram: Periodic Soil Moisture, Temperature, and Thaw Depth Measurements across Polygonal Tundra, Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska, 2014-2015
description: Manual measurements of soil moisture, temperature, and thaw depth were collected in the footprint of the NGEE Arctic Tram starting 2014-07-20 and continuing through 2015-07-16. There were 10 periodic sampling events with measurements in one *.csv file. These measurements were collected under the Tram observational platform. Probes were inserted into ground beneath the track closest to Tram sensors measurement locations at each Tram measurement position (Position # marked on the tracks). A MiniTrase Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) instrument was used to measure volumetric water content (VWC; units = m3/m3). Soil temperature was measured with a thermocouple probe. Depth of thawed soil was measured from the top of the moss layer or top of soil. See user guide for more information *.pdf.

The Next-Generation Ecosystem Experiments: Arctic (NGEE Arctic), was a research effort to reduce uncertainty in Earth System Models by developing a predictive understanding of carbon-rich Arctic ecosystems and feedbacks to climate. NGEE Arctic was supported by the Department of Energy's Office of Biological and Environmental Research.

The NGEE Arctic project had two field research sites: 1) located within the Arctic polygonal tundra coastal region on the Barrow Environmental Observatory (BEO) and the North Slope near Utqiagvik (Barrow), Alaska and 2) multiple areas on the discontinuous permafrost region of the Seward Peninsula north of Nome, Alaska.

Through observations, experiments, and synthesis with existing datasets, NGEE Arctic provided an enhanced knowledge base for multi-scale modeling and contributed to improved process representation at global pan-Arctic scales within the Department of Energy's Earth system Model (the Energy Exascale Earth System Model, or E3SM), and specifically within the E3SM Land Model component (ELM).

measurementTechnique:
These measurements are made by manually inserting a probe (thaw depth, moisture, and temperature) vertically into the ground; as compared to the automated measurements that consist of probes installed horizontally at the specified depths. Probes were inserted into ground beneath the outside track (remember cart rolls on two tracks like train; outside track would be closest to sensors) at each Tram Position (Position # marked on the tracks).
In this dataset, the surface for determining measurement depths was the top of either bare soil or the moss layer (they are synonymous in this case). If the sampling location was inundated with water, the measurements depths are recorded from soil/moss surface, not water surface.
We used the MiniTrase Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) instrument to measure volumetric water content (VWC; units = m3/m3).
Soil temperature was measured at 5 or 10 cm below the top of moss layer or top of soil using a thermocouple probe.

Manual vs. automated VWC measurements
The difference between automated probes and TDR instrument is the technology used to measure VWC and the subsequent calibration equations to convert electrical signals to % moisture. Both techniques are measuring the dielectric constant of the material surrounding the probe, but only the TDR outputs the absolute dielectric constant.
Missing data value code: “-9999”. Note that not all measurements were taken on a given event.
